The route still holds: parts/p15.tex:34 and annex/p15.tex:33 input the chapter and its annex, reached from main.tex:40 and main.tex:64.

The held Feller (p.54, after (9.15)) prints 'for n = 5 we get 120.01'. The chapter gives 120.003 (120.0026370861...), which is the correct value, but it does not note that this differs from the source's printed figure. The figure is not attributed to Feller, so this was not treated as a coverage failure.

thm:p15-weak-elementary-asymptotics also says it 'supplies source Lemma 3.1.1 and its Exercise 3.1.1 application', and thm:p15-weak-rademacher-example proves the fair-sign normal limit. C002 and C015 here claim the same Durrett 3.1 items, so two sections claim the same source items and any crosswalk must not credit them twice.

These are the thinnest local-to-global passages in the chapter. They name the Riemann-sum, cutoff and complement steps instead of writing out again the estimates given in full at annex 399-416 and 421-425. C013 states no summed-error bound. I judged them to be written steps because every case-specific estimate (uniform local bound, Chebyshev tail bound, point-mass bound) is stated and the generic mechanics are already written in the same annex. A stricter reviewer might call C013 lines 675-683 a sketch.
'the previously proved Gaussian integral' has no cross-reference. The result is thm:p15-normal-normalization (handbook/parts/p15/convolution-gamma-normal.tex:301), which comes earlier on the route.

Three steps are left implicit: the split of each factor into log(1-(j-1)/n)-log(1+j/n), the identity sum(2j-1)=k^2, and the requirement k<=n/2 that the |t|<=1/2 bound needs. The parallel derivation in handbook/annex/p15/weak-convergence-of-laws.tex:648-660 writes them out.
'The resulting lower bound grows faster than 12n+2' is asserted without an explicit inequality. The step is elementary.
The Feller locator 'II.9 ... pp. 51-54' includes p.51, which belongs to II.8 (formula (8.11), used in (9.9)). The page range is right, but the section label only covers pp. 52-54.
